title: Capstone: ship like First Mate
goal: Ship a small feature to a real repo through the full loop: spec, plan, parallel worktrees, tests first, three gates on the head commit, and a gated merge.
setup_cmd: cp -r exercises/ex-5-4-capstone/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-5-4-capstone && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-5-4-capstone && npm i && git init -b main && git add -A && git commit -m starter && gh repo create fm-capstone --public --source . --push

starter_prompts.claude: Read AGENTS.md, SPEC_TEMPLATE.md and PLAN_TEMPLATE.md. We are adding due dates to the todo library (README.md, section The feature). Stay in plan mode and do not edit code. First draft SPEC.md: numbered P0 acceptance criteria, exact function signatures, non-goals, and two workstreams with explicit file ownership so they cannot touch the same file. Show it to me before you write PLAN.md.
starter_prompts.codex: Read AGENTS.md, SPEC_TEMPLATE.md and PLAN_TEMPLATE.md. We are adding due dates to the todo library (README.md, section The feature). Do not edit code yet. First draft SPEC.md: numbered P0 acceptance criteria, exact function signatures, non-goals, and two workstreams with explicit file ownership so they cannot touch the same file. Show it to me before you write PLAN.md.

solution_notes: The spec fixes interfaces and per-workstream file ownership before anyone codes, so the two worktrees can never edit the same file and the merges are clean.
Tests come first and live on main. Workers turn them green and never weaken them, which is the same test-first rule this app was built under.
Every gate is a commit status on the exact reviewed SHA. Pushing anything after approval makes gate:merge refuse, so approval can never cover code nobody reviewed.
The UI/UX gate records 'N/A: no UI changes' rather than being skipped, so gate:merge still has all three statuses to check.
